subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Class Action Lawsuits
description: A quick, practical guide to Class Action Lawsuits.

hook.text: After the Equifax breach, 147 million people were eligible for compensation. Most got less than a dollar.

buildup.text: Class action lawsuits let millions of victims sue together. Lawyers negotiate settlements for the group.

discovery.text: Equifax settled for $700 million. After legal fees and 147 million claimants, individuals got almost nothing.

twist.text: The lawyers earned millions. The executives kept their bonuses. The victims got a credit monitoring coupon.

climax.text: Class actions punish companies on paper but rarely make individual victims whole.

punchline.text: Millions affected. Pennies per person. Justice?

quiz.question: Why do class action settlements often disappoint individual victims?
options: The settlement is split among millions, leaving pennies per person
Courts always side with the companies
Only the first 100 people to file get any money
